recap.workouts:
Lifting: five sessions, Monday to Friday.

Mon, Legs A: belt squat 120 lb, 10/8/8; leg extension 115 lb, 10/10; seated leg curl 65 lb, 12/12/11 (two more sets at 65 without reps). Your note: that is too many sets of leg curls, build from 3 this week. Noted and applied to next week.

Tue, Upper 1: incline DB press 70 lb, 12/12/10; cable chest fly 45 lb, 15/15 (top of the range, so it goes to 50); lateral raise 20 lb, 20/20/15; triceps pushdown 120 lb, 12/12/11.

Wed, Upper 2: lat pulldown 230 lb, 11/11/9; barbell row 85 lb, 12/10; face pull 95 lb, 20/20/20; barbell curl 65 lb, 12/10/10; overhead triceps extension 65 lb, 12/10.

Thu, Legs B: belt squat 120 lb, 9/8; glute raise on the hyper at bodyweight, 14/14; seated leg curl 45 lb, 20/20 (top of the range, so it goes to 50); leg extension 90 lb, 18/16. You noted back discomfort on the glute raise that day.

Fri, Upper 3: lateral raise 20 lb, 20/20; cable curl 40 lb, 12/12 (top of the range, so +5); triceps pushdown 135 lb, 15/15 (top of the range, so 145); face pull at 100 lb, reps not entered.

CrossFit: classes Monday to Friday. Mon: 145 on the first part, second part scaled (class RPE 4). Tue: 5 bar muscle-ups in one of the sets, medium intensity overall (RPE 4). Wed: single snatches building, then a couple of overhead squats instead of touch-and-go (RPE 5). Thu: mostly easy, 75 on the first exercise. Fri: 60 cal on the echo bike instead of the run, pushed the second echo bike piece to stay inside the time cap (RPE 4).

Endurance, what the watch recorded: Mon evening run, 54 min, average HR 124. Wed afternoon run, 27 min, average HR 140. Sat: a 38-minute road ride (no HR on that file), a 60-minute Cross Training activity at average HR 146, and a 55-minute walk at average HR 105.

The phone's last sync here was Friday morning, so Saturday and Sunday entries may not have reached this recap yet.
recap.takeaways:
Loads moved forward on the upper days: cable fly (to 50), cable curl (to 45), triceps pushdown (to 145) and seated leg curl (to 50 on Legs B) all hit the top of their rep range and earn the bump next time.

Face pull at 95 lb gave 20/20/20 on Wednesday, so it is ready to go up once Friday's 100 lb sets have reps logged. Entering reps on every set lets the engine see those triggers.

Five lifting sessions and five classes in the week, with belt squat holding at 120 lb on both leg days and lateral raise at 20/20 on Friday.

Your leg-curl note shaped next week: 3 sets per leg day, with the extra hamstring work moved to the glute raise on the hyper.

recapPrev.workouts:
CrossFit was Maple, the chipper: 60 cal echo bike, 20-inch step-ups, a 20 lb med-ball piece, 30 burpees, and 19 muscle-ups in place of the class's strict pull-ups, time-capped at 18 minutes. RPE 5 - a controlled effort, and the echo bike went closer to the men's TRAIN pace (60 cal) than the FITNESS scale the plan actually called for (50 cal). Hypertrophy was the pull + triceps + leg-maintenance day: lat pulldown 210x12/12, barbell row 85x8/9, face pull 95x15/16, barbell curl 65x10/10, overhead triceps extension 150x12 then a swap to French press at 45x12 for the second set, belt squats subbed for leg curls at 110x12, tibia raise 20x20/15. RPE 5. Nothing sore or flagged in your notes today.

Then the retest: CT31, moved here from Monday as you asked. Total time 60:05, and the 24-minute Zone 3 tune block held very steady - 224 W average, only 0.5% variation second to second, about as clean a pacing job as this block gets. Compliance came in at 110% of the planned load. Heart rate told a slightly different story: it settled at 161 for the block, two beats above the 159 bike LTHR that band was tested against, with a modest 4.2 bpm of drift over the 24 minutes and 3.2% decoupling - well inside the coupled range, so nothing like a blow-up, just running a shade hot at that output. tune.py read it as threshold likely down a touch (or just a harder day) and took the conservative nudge rather than a bigger correction - more in the takeaways below. One thing worth naming as a hypothesis and not a finding: this morning's Maple went a notch harder than the FITNESS call written for it (the higher echo-bike pace, muscle-ups for pull-ups), and while that call was written with a run in mind for this afternoon rather than the bike session that actually landed here, a few hours of residual load from a harder morning is a plausible, unprovable piece of why HR ran warm on the block. Tonight's automated deep-dive file for this ride hadn't generated by the time this recap ran, so this read comes from tune.py's own per-second analysis of the block rather than the full rep-by-rep stream report - a gap on the pipeline side, not in your effort.
recapPrev.takeaways:
Bike anchors moved for the first time since July: FTP 236 to 229 watts, bike LTHR unchanged at 159, run anchors untouched. This was a conservative nudge (confidence medium), not a big correction - HR sat two beats above LTHR at a very cleanly paced output, but drift and decoupling both stayed in the normal range. Worth watching whether the next tune confirms it or today was just a harder day.

Live hypothesis, not a verdict: an ambitious Maple this morning - Train-pace bike, muscle-ups - landing a few hours before the retest may have contributed to the warmer HR. Can't prove it from one day's data, but it's a pattern worth tracking if it shows up again.

No changes to the rest of the week - CrossFit, hypertrophy and the retest all landed as planned, nothing to absorb or reschedule.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
Wednesday is CrossFit only - travel day, no hypertrophy, no endurance. Save the legs and lungs for Thursday's full rest day. The class is a Clean & Jerk single build plus the metcon Oak: 15-12-9 deadlifts and jump-rope singles. Check the grip and the first pull off the floor on the warm-up, and how the legs feel walking into 36 deadlifts.

Barbell feeling good, ready to move? Build the clean and jerk briskly toward a strong, confident single - not a max hunt, that's off the table for the whole week regardless - and let Oak's deadlifts move with purpose.

Legs flat, everything feeling heavy? Keep the ladder light and technical, and let Oak's reps land at an easier, unhurried pace.

Both are a good day's work; this is a one-job travel day, not one to make or break.
